narrative.overview: A listing is a part, and the page shows it the way a component manufacturer would: a title block with a revision table, thin and double rules, numbered sections, tabular values, one header cell in solid ink. Structure comes from rules and aligned columns, never from fills, shadows or effects. Transition: only the landing hero is built in this direction; the header, footer, lower sections, dashboard, explore and product pages still ship the earlier Signal & Void system and are slated to be replaced.
keyCharacteristics: Ink on ground, one accent, one red, one green; no gradients, glow, shadows, photography or texture.
Square corners inside the sheet and the search; rules do the work of cards.
Three-column part with a double rule under its name row; a title-block table beside the headline from lg.
Geist for words, Geist Mono for values and commands, Estedad for Persian.
Static: no animation in the sheet; server-rendered markup that works without script.

rules.name: The One Accent Rule
rules.body: Accent is a mark, not a surface. It appears on the Search button, table header rule and numerals, and nowhere as a panel or background wash.

rules.name: The Red Means Absent Rule
rules.body: Red marks "not declared" and nothing else. It is never an error colour inside the sheet.

rules.name: The Strong-Rule Rule
rules.body: Outer frames and column dividers are ink at 60% (border-foreground/60); interior row dividers are the hairline token. Two weights, no third.

rules.name: The Mono Is Data Rule
rules.body: Geist Mono is for versions, hashes, commands and table values. Prose and filters stay in Geist. In Persian, non-Latin values fall back to Estedad.

rules.name: The Latin Island Rule
rules.body: Versions, document numbers, hashes and the command are wrapped dir=ltr so they hold their shape inside Persian text.

rules.name: The Ruled-Cell Rule
rules.body: Regions are separated by a rule and cell padding, not by gaps between floating boxes.

rules.name: The No-Decoration Rule
rules.body: Nothing in the sheet exists only to look good: no icon without a function, no fill without information, no ornament. The pin diagram is the only drawing, and it states compatibility.

rules.name: The Example-Is-Labelled Rule
rules.body: Synthetic content is named as such twice, in the tag cell and in the footer. Never show a made-up listing as real.

rules.name: The State-Absence Rule
rules.body: Undeclared is printed, never omitted: a parameter with no declaration keeps its row, shows a dash or a red "not declared" mark, and is never hidden.

dos: Do build new sheet surfaces from the existing theme tokens only: ink, ground, hairline, --muted, --primary, --destructive, --verified.
Do use the two rule weights: border-foreground/60 for structure, border-border for rows.
Do set values and commands in Geist Mono, wrapped in dir="ltr", and give Persian its own face and no tracking.
Do number sections with accent mono numerals and put labels at 11px, 0.08em, uppercase.
Do keep the sheet static and readable without JavaScript; targets at least 24px (shortcuts 32px, buttons 44px).
Do print "not declared" rows and mark examples as examples.
donts: Don't use gradients, glow, shadows, blur, photography or textures on the datasheet, and don't reintroduce the nebula or a gradient headline.
Don't round the corners of the sheet or the hero search.
Don't use accent as a panel, card or background fill, or red for anything but absence.
Don't hide undeclared rows, or ship an unlabelled example.

Don't extend Signal & Void for new surfaces: the Plasma large-area primary, Newsreader .editorial headings, pill chips, --shadow-*/--glow-* and the long motion tokens remain elsewhere and are slated to be replaced.
Don't treat the hero search's carried remnants (suggestions dropdown shape and shadow, placeholder typing, lucide glyphs) as part of the datasheet system.
